title: Minimal Offline Runtime Shrinkwrap and Operator Guide
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document defines the shrinkwrap packaging model for minimal offline Redwood runtime images and provides a field-operator playbook for installation, verification, day-2 tuning, and safe rollbacks in air-gapped or VPC-isolated customer environments. 'Shrinkwrap' in this context means a cryptographically verifiable bundle containing only the runtime binaries, model artifacts (optional), minimal OS bits, and an operator manifest that includes acceptance and telemetry contracts.

Audience
- Field operators performing on-prem installs
- SRE/Platform engineers responsible for on-prem rollouts
- Security/compliance reviewers validating evidence packages

Goals
- Produce a small, auditable offline bundle that can be installed without internet access.
- Ensure operators can validate integrity and provenance before one-touch installation.
- Minimize attack surface and required maintenance steps for customers without continuous connectivity.

Non-goals
- This guide does not cover large-scale multi-zone private fleets or full multi-tenant orchestration. See reference-architectures for those topologies.

Prerequisites
1) Customer environment: air-gapped or restricted egress VPC with out-of-band operator terminal.
2) Operator laptop with cosign v1.10+ or GPG v2.2+, access to the customer-provided KMS/HSM public attestation key.
3) Minimum hardware profile defined in the manifest. (Operators must verify hardware serials and firmware baselines.)

Shrinkwrap artifact model (high level)
- manifest.json.sig            -> signed manifest (cosign or GPG)
- manifest.json                -> shrinkwrap manifest (checksums, image tags, requirements)
- runtime.tgz                 -> runtime binaries and systemd units (sha256)
- kernel-mods.tgz             -> optional signed kernel modules required for GPU/IB driver integration
- model.<name>.tar.zst         -> optional model bundles (per customer license)
- evidence/                    -> compliance evidence: SBOM, signing certs, build logs, provenance.json

Example: shrinkwrap manifest (YAML snippet)
---
version: 1
bundle_id: redwood-runtime-shrinkwrap-2026-02
runtime_image: redwood-runtime-0.9.3-linux-x86_64.tgz
hardware_minimum:
  cpu_cores: 16
  memory_gb: 64
  nvme_gb: 500
  gpus: [A10G]
required_kernel: 5.15.0-58-generic
services:
  - name: rw-allocator
    unit: rw-allocator.service
    ports: [50051]
telemetry_contract:
  sampling_rate_percent: 1
  max_payload_bytes: 512
sbom: sbom.spdx.json
provenance: provenance.json
---

Verification (integrity & provenance)
Operators must perform the following checks before any install. Failure to validate any of these must trigger an escalation to the release owner.

1) Verify binary signature (recommended: cosign). Example:

# verify signature (cosign)
cosign verify-blob --key /path/to/customer_pubkey.pem --signature manifest.json.sig manifest.json

2) Compare checksums in manifest to local files. Example:

sha256sum -c manifest-checksums.txt

3) Validate SBOM and provenance: ensure build_id and git commit match the allowed list in the evidence folder.

Secure install checklist (field operator)
- [ ] Confirm operator identity (MFA) and create installation incident/tracking ticket.
- [ ] Physically verify hardware serials and firmware hashes against manifest.hardware_firmware_hashes.
- [ ] Run signature verification (cosign/GPG).
- [ ] Copy artifacts to pre-approved host (isolated ingress node).
- [ ] Install kernel-mods in maintenance window and verify module signatures.
- [ ] Deploy runtime.tgz to /opt/redwood/runtime and set ownership to rw-runtime:rw-runtime.
- [ ] Enable systemd units: rw-allocator.service, rw-runtime.service, rw-healthwatch.service.

Installation commands (example)

# unpack and install
sudo tar -C /opt -xzf runtime.tgz
sudo chown -R rw-runtime:rw-runtime /opt/redwood/runtime
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable --now rw-allocator.service rw-runtime.service rw-healthwatch.service

Runtime boot verification
- Check systemd health: systemctl status rw-runtime.service
- Health endpoint: curl --unix-socket /var/run/rw-runtime.sock http://localhost/healthz
- Expected response: {"status":"ok","kv_cache": "cold"} on first boot.

Day-2 operational runbook (first 48 hours)
1) Telemetry acceptance: validate that sampling_rate_percent in manifest matches telemetry.ingest rate on the operator console. Target: 1% sampling of token-level traces; spike cap 5% for 15 minutes max.
2) KV cache warmup: execute kv-warmup --prefixes=/common/prompt-sets --concurrency=8 --target-rate=50rps to prefill the in-memory cache for canonical prompt sets. Monitor evictions via /metrics (rw_kvcache_evictions_total).
3) Load testing (smoke): run internal-synthetic-suite with the customer-provided traffic-mix profile at 10% of expected peak for 30 minutes. Verify latency SLOs (P95 <= 250ms for short-sequence routes).
4) Resource tuning: adjust systemd slice CPUQuota and MemoryLimit, if OOMs or throttling are observed. Recommended default slice overrides in /etc/systemd/system/rw-runtime.slice.d/10-limits.conf:

[Slice]
CPUQuota=80%
MemoryLimit=56G

Telemetry and observability contract (required evidence)
Operators must verify these metrics are being emitted to the local aggregator (or retained locally in evidence bundle if required):
- rw_runtime_uptime_seconds (gauge)
- rw_inflight_requests (gauge)
- rw_token_throughput_total (counter)
- rw_kvcache_hits_total / rw_kvcache_misses_total (counters)
- rw_model_load_time_seconds (histogram)

Sampling/Retention guidance table
| metric | default sampling | retention on-device | notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| traces | 1% | 72h | Burst cap 5% for 15m |
| metrics (high cardinality) | 100% aggregated | 14d (summary) | raw histograms kept 7d |
| logs | severity>=WARN | 30d | structured JSON with event_id |

Upgrade and rollback procedure (stateless runtime patch)
This applies to small upgrades of the runtime binaries or configuration where the runtime is stateless and models are pinned. For stateful KV migrations see the separate migration playbook.

Planned upgrade (recommended flow)
1) Create change ticket and notify customer POC and SRE on-call.
2) Upload signed shrinkwrap to ingress node and run local verification steps.
3) Take a nightly maintenance window snapshot (file-system snapshot + tar + sha256). Store snapshot in evidence/archive/<date>.
4) Stop rw-allocator.service (graceful drain: rwctl drain --timeout 120s).
5) Apply new runtime.tgz and systemd unit changes.
6) Start services and run smoke-runner for 15 minutes. Validate metrics and health.
7) If checks pass, mark upgrade complete in ticket and record provenance.

Emergency rollback (if post-upgrade P95 latency regression or error rate > 2% sustained for 5m)
1) Initiate rollback runbook and add incident tag.
2) Run rwctl failover --mode=drain-local to switch traffic to fallback pool (if configured).
3) Stop current services: sudo systemctl stop rw-runtime.service rw-allocator.service
4) Reinstall last-known-good snapshot from evidence/archive/<date>.tar.gz and verify checksums.
5) Start services and monitor metrics for 10 minutes. If recovery fails, escalate to release-engineering and customer-ops.

Security & signing notes
- All runtime binaries are signed at build time using the Redwood build COSIGN key. For customer air-gap installs we provide a dedicated cosign public key in the evidence bundle for validation.
- Kernel module signing: all kernel modules are signed and verified via /usr/bin/kmodsign; require module.sig present.
- SBOM is provided as SPDX JSON and must be retained for 365 days in customer evidence retention for regulated customers.

Operator troubleshooting quick hits
- If service fails to start: check journalctl -u rw-runtime.service -n 200. Common causes: missing GPU driver, incorrect cgroup limits, or stale kv-cache directory permission.
- High cold-start rate: confirm kv-warmup completed and check rw_kvcache_misses_total. Increase warmup concurrency in small increments (+2).
- Telemetry not shipping: ensure local aggregator (rw-tele-collector) is running and sampling configuration in /etc/rw/telemetry.yaml matches manifest. Example telemetry.yaml: 

endpoint: file:///var/opt/rw/telemetry/archive
sampling_percent: 1
max_payload_bytes: 512

Ownership and escalation contacts
- Field install owner: Sophia Ramos (sophia@redwood.example.com)
- Release engineering on-call: #release-eng on Slack (paging policy in pagerduty)
- Security contact: sec-ops@redwood.example.com (for signature/attestation issues)

Acceptance evidence to collect (deliver to customer & Redwood compliance)
1) install.log (stdout of install run)
2) signature-verify.log (cosign/GPG output)
3) system snapshot sha256 and tarball reference (evidence/archive/<timestamp>.tar.gz)
4) telemetry sample extract (first 4 hours) and a short report validating sampling rates
5) SBOM and provenance.json

Related pages and references
- See: /confluence/eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/airgap-packaging-and-day2-hardening-2026 for airgap ingress patterns
- Build provenance standard: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/release-notes/provenance-policy
- Migration playbook (stateful): /confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/stateless-stateful-migration-and-cutover-guidelines-2026

Appendix A — Example cosign verification script
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail
PK=/opt/evidence/customer_pubkey.pem
if ! cosign verify-blob --key "$PK" --signature manifest.json.sig manifest.json; then
  echo "signature verification failed"
  exit 2
fi
sha256sum -c manifest-checksums.txt
echo "verification complete"

Appendix B — Minimal acceptance checklist (one-page)
1) Signatures verified
2) SBOM present and matched
3) Services start and healthcheck passes (10m)
4) Telemetry sample present (first 30m)
5) Smoke test P95 <= 250ms
6) Snapshot archived and checksum recorded
